title: maDMP project config
description: One self-contained project config (configs/projects/<id>.yaml — the filename must be the declared id). Strict: every field required, none extra — a typo like `rule:` or a missing `rules` fails validation at load time instead of deep in generation. Fields are grouped as the config file reads them: the project's own facts, then the rules it is built from, then what the generated DSW packages carry.

id.description: The project's one machine name, declared once and repeated nowhere: the filename this config sits at, its destination folder in the dmp-registry (and the ?project= routing key), and what the KM, the document template, the seed and the DSW baseline project are named after. The pattern is also, and independently, what DSW asks of a kmId (lowercase, digits, dashes) — it is the middle third of `organizationId:id:version`.

name.description: What a reader sees, and only that: the DSW package name, the KM title, and the registry meta.yaml. Free-form on purpose — deriving it from `id` would give `Socib Hf Radar`.

version.description: The project's version, bumped to publish a change. Semver X.Y.Z, and the form is DSW's rather than ours: with `organizationId` and `id` it composes the package identifier `organizationId:id:version` that dsw/common.package_id sends. Checked here so a malformed version fails at load time instead of on the last call of the pipeline, against a remote server.

rules.description: Pinned rules versions, base first: [{standard: version}, ...] -> rules/standards/<standard>/<version>.json. One key per entry, and both halves are the ones the rules file itself declares: the standard in the same snake_case rules.schema.json requires of it, the version as a non-empty string (unquoted 1.0 would be a YAML float, not a version).

organizationId.description: The DSW organization the generated packages belong to. Lowercase, digits and dots — DSW's own character set for the first third of `organizationId:id:version`. See `version` for why the form is checked here.
